questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Tasmania as my preferred destination due to the similarities between the Danish and Australian health care systems and because of the language. Also I was very interested in exploring the beautiful nature in Tasmania.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I will highly recommend going on exchange to Tasmania if you want to experience parts of the Australian nature and culture in small and a safe environment.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I received information via email from a contact person at University of Tasmania and found the rest of the information on their website and with the help from other students who had been on exchange. In the beginning, it was a bit overwhelming with all the new information but it was manageable.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: My contact person at University of Tasmania met me one of the first days upon my arrival which was a great help. She showed me the hospital and made sure that all my registrations, IT logins ect. were ok.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I rented a room in a 4-person dorm on campus. It was also possible to rent a 1-person apartment on campus.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: The dorm included a shared kitchen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I would highly recommend living on campus in a shared dorm. In this way, you'll meet other students and will be able to participate in the many events on campus. However, it is a bit more expensive that finding housing on your own.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registrations process was quite extensive and you'll have to spend a decent amount of time doing it - however it is still worth doing!

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: For the registration you'll have to send a lot of documents, fill out forms from the university and hospital and send a photo. I was very surprised that your ID-documents needed to be signed by an Australian Notary. It is quite expensive but needs to be done.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I received most of the information via email from a contact person at University of Tasmania. It explained most of the process but I also needed help from other students who have been on exchange.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful! I was able to do the clinical rotation as I wished for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The registration process may seem a bit overwhelming in the beginning. Break it down step by step and ask for help a the host university, your own university or ask other students who have been on exchange. Even though it'll take quite some time and money, it is definitely worth all the work!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did a 3-month clinical rotation at Department of General Surgery at Royal Hobart Hospital as a part of my 11th semester of the master of Medicine.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: As a medical student, be aware that the way of teaching in Australia is slightly different that in the Danish health care system. The students in Australia is a bit more passive at the ward and spend a lot of the time observing. As always you'll need to reach out to get involved and to get an opportunity to improve your pratical skills - this is even more important as an exchange student. Except this, the style of teaching resembles the style at the Danish hospitals.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: 3-month clinical rotation at Department of General Surgery at Royal Hobart Hospital

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend spending a part of your clinical rotation at the Emergency Department. My experience is that you'll be able to practice your clinical skills better here since the students in the Emergency Department often get the opportunity to see their own patients. 
The other part of the rotation, I would spend on one or more of the different wards at the hospital. Here you get the opportunity to learn more about a specific department and experience how the doctors work at the ward.

questions.answer: The "cost of living" is much comparable to Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was very surprised by the many events that were organized by the university.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Cooking classes, sports classes, day trips in the weekend, a dinner for all the students living on campus ever 14th day.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would highly recommend participating in as many activities arranged by the university as possible. It is a great way to meet other students and to experience Tasmania.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Especially the day trips arranged by the student organization TUSA are a great way to meet new friends and explore Tasmania in a cheaper way.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy - the culture is not very different from back home. Australians are very friendly and openminded.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open minded and catch all opportunities to participate in social events.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not experience any challenging cultural differences.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How friendly and open minded Australians are.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Reach out for every opportunity to learn at the hospital.
Participate in the social events arranged by the university.
Explore the stunning nature in your weekends.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It can be difficult to connect with the other medical exchange students at the hospital. Ask your contact person at the hospital or the other students. If possible, try to start your exchange in the beginning of July to make sure that you're a part of the introduction week at the university. Here you'll receive good information and meet a lot of people.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange was to live 3 months in a country so far away from home. It is a great way to gain more self-confidence and to get a new perspective on yourself and your everyday life back home. Also it has been very interesting to experience another health care system and compare it to the Danish health care system. Last, it has improved my skills in professional communication in English.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was to get used to being far away from family and friends for a decent amount of time. Make sure to participate in social events, meet other students and make new friendships!

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I highly recommend going on exchange and studying a semester abroad. It'll be an experience of a lifetime! :)

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
